findings.text: non-blocking: `assert exit_.value.code == lw.REFUSED_ENGINE_STATUS` compares the refusal's exit status against the same module constant the implementation raises (imas_ambix/agent/llm_watch.py:815 `raise SystemExit(REFUSED_ENGINE_STATUS)`), so the two sides move together. The guard is real -- deleting the refusal makes pytest.raises see no SystemExit -- but it pins no number: a change of imas_ambix/agent/llm_watch.py:102 from 2 to 1, which would make the refusal indistinguishable from a render failure -- the separability the constant's own comment claims -- leaves the suite green while the landed fragment states the refusal exits 2. The literal from the done_when's source (dotfiles bin/gpu-watch is not involved here; the value is this view's own) is what would have to appear on one side.

non-blocking: the `served is None` branch at imas_ambix/agent/llm_watch.py:180-182 is exercised by no test. The single test drives a document whose lane names an engine, so only the mismatch message is covered; the refusal a document naming no engine produces -- and the branch is load-bearing, because without it the same call falls through to `this view serves None only`, claiming an engine id of None -- is asserted nowhere, although docs/evidence/fragments/serving-across-servers/llm-watch-view.html states that behaviour as landed.
